messages:
jamal-support: Heads up — Acme reports the month-end totals don't match. Dashboard shows 42,183 tokens for Feb but the invoice line is 52,401. They're escalated and asking for a breakdown. cc @olivia-fin @sam-eng :eyes:

olivia-fin: Thanks. Can you paste invoice ID, account id, and billing window so I can pull raw usage?

jamal-support: Invoice INV-202402-8873, account: acme-corp-88, billing window: 2024-02-01 to 2024-02-28. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood/acme/usage?range=2024-02

sam-eng: Quick hypotheses: 1) aggregation cutoff mismatch (dashboard uses UTC snapshot) 2) tokenization/invoice counting includes system/tool outputs we might not show on dashboard 3) late ingestion events that made it into billing but not the snapshot.

maria-cs: Customer insists they didn't see any late spikes. I'll pull their exported CSV now.

billing-bot: Usage export ready: s3://redwood-exports/acme-corp-88/usage_export_1719124000.csv

jamal-support: I pulled the export and found a big spike right at month end. Example snippet: `usage_record_id=ur_zz123 tokens_total=10000 model=redwood-xl recorded_at=2024-02-28T23:58:12Z`

sam-eng: Can you paste the raw rows around 2024-02-28T23:5xZ so I can check ingest vs snapshot timestamps?

jamal-support: Pasting a few lines from the export:
```
ur_zz123, acme-corp-88, 2024-02-28T23:58:12Z, 10000, completion
ur_zz124, acme-corp-88, 2024-03-01T00:00:05Z, 50, prompt
ur_zz125, acme-corp-88, 2024-03-01T00:00:20Z, 500, completion
```

sam-eng: That helps. Two things to check: the account-level billing_cutoff timezone and the dashboard snapshot cutoff. Many accounts use UTC but some have local-time overrides. If invoice generator uses account-local cutoff, records near midnight can be bucketed differently.

olivia-fin: Confirmed: acme-corp-88 has billing_cutoff set to PST (account override). Dashboard snapshots are taken in UTC. That would move late-Feb UTC events into the Feb invoice when translated to PST.

maria-cs: The customer says the extra 10,218 tokens on their Feb invoice match the spike(s) in the export.

sam-eng: Running reconciliation queries now. Steps I'm using:
1) UTC-window sum: SELECT SUM(tokens) FROM usage WHERE account='acme-corp-88' AND recorded_at BETWEEN '2024-02-01T00:00:00Z' AND '2024-02-28T23:59:59Z';
2) Billing-window sum (account cutoff): same but convert recorded_at to PST cutoff.

jamal-support: Customer is anxious — can we acknowledge and give an interim explanation?

olivia-fin: Draft reply: "We're investigating a classification mismatch between the usage dashboard (UTC snapshot) and the invoice (account-local cutoff). We're reconciling at token level and will issue a credit if we find a billing error." I'll send this to the customer now.

sam-eng: Results: UTC-sum = 42,183; billing-cutoff-sum = 52,401. Delta ~= 10,218 which matches ur_zz123 + related records. Root cause: account-local billing_cutoff (PST) + dashboard snapshot time difference. The spike was ingested after the dashboard snapshot but before invoice generation as translated to PST.

maria-cs: Action items?

sam-eng: Engineering: ENG-7892 to align dashboard snapshot windows with billing generator or add a flag to show account-level cutoff on the UI. Short-term: finance should issue a credit for the delta and mark the account so we don't double-bill in March.

olivia-fin: I'll create the credit memo and notify billing-ops. Preparing CM-202402-8873.

billing-bot: Credit memo created: CM-202402-8873, offset tokens: 10,218, assigned_to=olivia-fin

jamal-support: Customer update sent. They appreciated the quick acknowledgement; asked for the final reconciliation tomorrow morning.

sam-eng: I'll file the engineering task and include unit tests for cutoff translation logic. Also recommending an in-console banner when account has non-UTC billing_cutoff so CS can preemptively explain month-end diffs.

maria-cs: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread open until reconciliation confirmed.
